incident-bot: [PAGER] Auth anomaly detected on proxy cluster pxy-3 (us-west-2). Persistent 401s + session "ghosting" pattern starting ~2026-03-17T02:12Z. Incident id INC-9501. Paging @alex-oncall @maria-sec for on-call + security.

alex-oncall: Ack :rotating_light: pulling logs and checking recent deploys.

alex-oncall: Running quick query against auth logs:
`SELECT src_ip, count(*) FROM auth_logs WHERE proxy=\"pxy-3\" AND status=401 GROUP BY src_ip ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 10;`
Top offenders: 185.62.34.12, 185.62.34.13, 185.62.34.14 repeated across sessions.

sam-sre: Seeing same spike in metrics (rate ~400 r/s to /v1/session/validate). User-Agent often shows `curl/7.92 (bot)` and no consistent cookie.

maria-sec: Can we confirm token reuse across different IPs (i.e., session_id replay)? Ask for KV cache and request headers dump for those session_ids.

alex-oncall: Quick grep: `grep -E \"session_id=[a-z0-9-]+\" /var/log/proxy/pxy-3/*.log | awk -F\"session_id=\" '{print $2}' | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head`
Output shows the same session IDs appearing from multiple src_ips -> likely replay/ghosting.

sam-sre: I'm applying immediate mitigation: adding iptables block for the /24s we see and a WAF rule for the UA pattern. Command: `sudo iptables -A INPUT -s 185.62.34.0/24 -j DROP` (applied on pxy-3). Deploying WAF rule id waf-9892 to drop requests to /v1/session/validate with UA matching `curl/*(bot)`

deploy-bot: null-route applied to pxy-3 (control-plane id cfg-7821).

sam-sre: Also tightened rate-limits for unauthenticated session endpoints (burst=20, sustained=5r/s).

maria-sec: Requesting emergency rotation of session-store encryption keys & service tokens for svc-token-prod1. If logs show session fragments were written to object store, assume exposure until proven otherwise. Please coordinate with dev-platform.

dev-platform: We'll rotate the encryption keys for session-store and issue new tokens for svc-token-prod1. ETA ~20m. We'll also run a targeted token revocation sweep for suspicious session IDs.

support: Drafting customer-facing message: "We experienced elevated authentication errors for some customers in us-west-2. We have mitigations in place and are performing a security sweep. We will notify affected customers if we confirm exposure." Ready to send after rotation and initial impact check.

alex-oncall: Monitoring shows 401 spike dropped back to baseline after IP blocks and WAF. No downstream deploys in last hour that would explain the spike. Collecting full logs for sec.

maria-sec: Please check S3 forwarder uploads for any log snapshots around 02:12-02:20. Run: `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-logs-staging/pxy-3/2026-03-17/`

alex-oncall: Found one upload `auth_dumps/pxy-3-02-13.log.gz` (2.1MB) from forwarder service at 02:13. Downloading and scanning now. Preliminary: contains truncated session_id fragments and headers; no clear PII but treat as potential exposure.

legal: Looping in legal to assess notification threshold and regulator obligations.

alex-oncall: Immediate action items: 1) complete key/token rotation (dev-platform) 2) revoke suspicious session IDs and issue forced reauth for impacted sessions 3) finish customer comms (support/legal) 4) collect full audit and hand to security for forensics.

maria-sec: Agreed. After rotation + revocation, run a replay test against a quarantined proxy to validate mitigations.

alex-oncall: Closing pager for now (mitigations active). Channel remains open for follow-ups and postmortem scheduling. :white_check_mark:
